No. In the matched C2D1 cohort (73 patients with both CyTOF and Olink data), circulating immune-cell frequencies did not significantly correlate with serum protein levels after multiple-testing correction.

I tested all 16 available C2D1 cell-frequency × serum-protein pairs using Spearman correlation and BH-FDR correction. No pooled association was significant (0/16 raw p<0.05; 0/16 q<0.05). The strongest pooled trends were weak negative correlations between CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells and CXCL9 (rho=-0.233, p=0.0615, q=0.535, n=65) and CXCL10 (rho=-0.222, p=0.0756, q=0.535, n=65).

Arm-stratified analyses also found no FDR-significant correlations. The most notable exploratory signal was in Arm C2: HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells vs IFN-γ (rho=-0.588, p=0.0050, q=0.080, n=21), but it did not survive FDR correction.

Conclusion: the available C2D1 data do not support validated correlations between the measured circulating immune-cell frequencies and selected serum proteins. Any nominal arm-specific trends should be treated as hypothesis-generating only.
